clue.text: Gossip about king following new direction in dance

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the earlier-read piece is placed second

parts.note: a zig is a sudden sharp turn onto a new course

indicators.note: to be about something is to go round it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: ana is a collection of someone's table talk and gossip
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone spreads gossip about a monarch who has taken up a new style of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ana, a collection of someone's table talk, is a crossword favourite for gossip. A zig is a sharp change of course, hence a new direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A ziganka is a Russian country dance performed to quick music, so it is a specific example of a dance.

clue.text: Ginger's family relish live competition hosted by Zidane, every so often

parts.note: zing is zest or relish

indicators.note: a host takes a guest inside, so the guest letters sit within the host's
doing something every so often means at regular gaps, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of the footballer's name
to be is to live or exist
a race is a competition

explanation.surface: A redhead's relatives enjoy a lively contest put on by the French footballer Zinedine Zidane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' looks like a red-haired person, but it is the plant. The footballer's name supplies only its second, fourth and sixth letters, which then open to house the contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Zingiberaceae is the botanical family name of the ginger plants, which includes turmeric and cardamom as well.

clue.text: Plant oil or accompaniment for it? Grunt carrying one litre

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: 'it' is Italian vermouth, drunk in gin and it
a grunt is a US infantryman, a GI
Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: A question whether this is a cooking oil or a mixer, followed by a soldier lugging a litre bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' reads as a pronoun for the oil, but it is Italian vermouth, whose classic partner in the bar is gin. GI holding I and L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingili is another name for sesame oil, pressed from the seeds of the sesame plant and used in Indian cooking.

clue.text: Musk maybe worn by instigator of unruly uprising in crown, as Edmund has it

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from bottom to top, the opposite way
worn things and their wearers are bound together, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Elon Musk is an example of someone with that surname
the first letter of 'unruly'

explanation.surface: A tech billionaire seems to be stirring rebellion against the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund is Edmund Spenser, the Elizabethan poet whose spellings the clue tells you to use. NOLE with U set inside gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noule is Spenser's spelling of noll, an old word for the head or the top of the head.

clue.text: Fruitless moan over entering part of Oceania briefly

indicators.note: whatever enters goes inside, so these letters sit within others
a brief form is cut short, so a long place name is reduced to its abbreviation

parts.note: Australia, shortened to its abbreviation
to carp is to complain or moan
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A grumble about something futile spreads across the Pacific region.
explanation.walkthrough: Oceania covers Australia and the Pacific islands; Australia's short form is the part meant. Over is the cricket sense, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: Acarpous is a botanical term for plants that bear no fruit, so it literally means fruitless.

clue.text: French singer scoffed, not finishing manoeuvre in manège

indicators.note: something left unfinished stops short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Édith Piaf, the French chanteuse
scoffed means ate greedily, FED, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A French chanteuse sneered and failed to complete a movement at the riding school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' reads as mocked, but here it means gobbled, FED. A manège is a riding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A piaffe is a dressage movement, a slow trot on the spot, taught to horses in the riding school.

clue.text: European dons Roman mantle in the Spanish Main?

indicators.note: to don clothing is to put it on and be inside it, so one piece is wrapped

parts.note: a palla was a mantle worn by Roman women
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European puts on a Roman cloak while sailing the Caribbean waters once held by Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish Main was the Spanish-ruled Caribbean coast; read differently it is a main course from Spain, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella, the saffron rice dish from Valencia, is the best-known Spanish main course, a cheeky reading of a historical phrase.

clue.text: Surreal age — I end up having reptilian body parts

indicators.note: something surreal is dreamlike and distorted, so the letters are rearranged out of their natural order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone muses on living in strange times and fearing they will turn out like a lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end up' looks like part of the surface's grammar, but every letter of 'age I end up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguipede means snake-footed, describing mythical giants whose legs ended in serpents, so their limbs were reptilian.

clue.text: Ross's confused lover, by lake, bitten by fly

parts.note: a fan is a devotee or lover of something

indicators.note: a bite closes jaws around something, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a ked is the sheep fly or sheep tick
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A man named Ross has a muddled sweetheart who got bitten by insects beside a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross is not a person but Ross-shire, a Highland county, signalling a Scots word. The fly is the sheep ked, a wingless parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: Fankled is Scots for tangled or entangled, so in Scotland it describes something muddled up and confused.

clue.text: Swear Clare possibly swallowed drinking vessel

parts.note: a Poor Clare is a member of an order of nuns
a cup is a drinking vessel
swallowed food, so ate

explanation.surface: Someone curses because a woman called Clare gulped down a whole tankard.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare looks like a woman's name, but the Poor Clares are an order of nuns founded by St Clare. The pieces come in the order NUN, CUP, ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nuncupate is to declare solemnly by word of mouth, as with a spoken will or vow, so it means to swear.

clue.text: Stateside rotter touching IT user's picture frames

indicators.note: a frame surrounds what it holds, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a GIF is a computer image file
on means touching or resting against

explanation.surface: An American scoundrel lays hands on a computer user's framed photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: Stateside means in American usage. The picture is the image file format, which wraps round the word for touching after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gonif is American slang, from Yiddish, for a thief or rascal, which matches a rotter or scoundrel.

clue.text: Counterfeiter penning Slavic novel, article and set of Victorian letters

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in an enclosure, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a forger counterfeits documents or money

indicators.note: novel means new and original, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A faker is writing a Slavic novel along with an essay and a bundle of nineteenth-century correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' and 'letters' both pose as literature; 'novel' is really the anagram signal. The title is Latin, roughly 'Fortune the club-bearer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fors Clavigera was John Ruskin's series of open letters to the workmen of Britain, published through the 1870s.

clue.text: Egg on the first person making a reactive compound

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun
egg is old military slang for a bomb or mine

explanation.surface: Urging on the leader produces a volatile mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' reads as urge, but 'Egg' is slang for an explosive and 'on' places it after I in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An imine is an organic chemical with a carbon-nitrogen double bond, an intermediate that reacts readily.

clue.text: Like a cushion turned up by residence, taken in both hands

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something taken in is received inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right hands
a villa is a large residence

explanation.surface: A cushion is plumped up at a house and carried in with two hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads as a phrasal verb, but only 'turned' acts on the little word after it. Both hands are left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulvillar is the adjective from pulvillus, a small cushion or pad such as on an insect's foot.

clue.text: Formerly distinguished compiler's coming in without bits of information by The Times

indicators.note: whatever comes in ends up inside, so these letters sit within others

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
the setter speaking: compiler's means I am, I'M
binary bits are ones and zeros, written as letters I and O
a newspaper refers to itself as us, the editorial we

explanation.surface: A once-famous setter turns up at the office without any news to offer the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Binary digits one and zero pass for the letters I and O. 'Formerly' marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Eximious is an obsolete word for excellent or eminent, so in older writing it described someone distinguished.

clue.text: Footprint of yours truly in Berlin certainly not by broken tile

parts.note: ich is German for I

indicators.note: something broken has its parts disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a firm refusal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist in Berlin swears the footprint left beside a cracked tile is not theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yours truly' means the speaker, I, which in German is ICH. 'by' simply places the rearranged TILE next.
explanation.definitionFit: An ichnolite is a fossil footprint, or a stone bearing one, preserved in rock.

clue.text: Dine out, entertained by eg ladies from Slavic set

indicators.note: a host entertains guests inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: the ladies is a lavatory, a WC

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of women from Eastern Europe host a dinner party at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies' looks like the guests, but it is the women's lavatory, abbreviated as a water closet.
explanation.definitionFit: Wendic is the language group of the Wends, a Slavic people of eastern Germany, so it names a Slavic group.

clue.text: Rector's beginning to cut cost over academic work, making helpful ruling on course

indicators.note: a cut goes into something, so this letter enters the middle of another word

parts.note: a fee is a cost

indicators.note: a beginning is the start of a word, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: beginning of 'Rector'
a doctor, abbreviated Dr, is an academic
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A rector starts trimming spending on scholarly research, issuing a useful course directive.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' just puts the first part above the second. The course is a golf course, not an academic one.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a free drop lets a player move the ball from an obstruction without penalty, a ruling that helps them.

clue.text: Haggard female votes for a bit of a laugh

parts.note: ayes are votes in favour
ha is one syllable of laughter

explanation.surface: A worn-out woman casts her ballot just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' reads as weary-looking, but it is the novelist H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayesha is the immortal queen in Rider Haggard's novel She, so she is the novelist's famous female character.

clue.text: Many a fine, upright character aboard vehicle that lady holds up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading from bottom to top
being aboard means riding inside, so one letter is put within another piece

parts.note: she is the pronoun for that lady

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the letter I is a single upright stroke

explanation.surface: A woman holds up a car carrying several decent, upstanding people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' reads as an adjective, but it is a penalty, and 'Many a' makes the answer plural. Two containers nest before the whole is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An eriach was a fine paid in early Irish law as compensation for murder, so eriachs are many such fines.

clue.text: Vessel filled with claret wine US lawman knocked back to begin with

indicators.note: this says the piece is placed at the start, ahead of the other
knocked back means sent backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Wyatt Earp, the Wild West lawman
cava is Spanish sparkling wine

explanation.walkthrough: 'claret' looks like the wine, but it is slang for blood, so the vessel is a blood vessel. The reversed lawman comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The praecava is the superior vena cava, the large vein carrying blood to the heart, so it is a blood vessel.

clue.text: Latin American lover sullen when drug-free, in the grip of sober people

indicators.note: free of a drug means it has been removed, so the letter for ecstasy goes
being gripped means held tightly within, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members stay sober
morose means sullen; without E, the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A sulky Latin lover who has given up drugs is held up by fellow members of a recovery group.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy; MOROS then sits inside AA.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorosa is the feminine of amoroso, a Spanish and Italian word borrowed for a lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Saving diamonds, cover armour in bits of metal

parts.note: a lid is a cover
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds, the letter removed
mail is chain armour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' reads as rescuing, but it means excepting, so the diamonds are taken out of the cover rather than kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Limail is an old word for metal filings, the small fragments rubbed off by a file.

clue.text: Kind of rock record I perform with eg Google or YouTube

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
taken as written
to do is to perform
both are examples of websites

explanation.surface: A musician talks about cutting a rock record and promoting it online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like the music genre, but it is a geological rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidosite is a metamorphic rock made mostly of the minerals epidote and quartz, so it is a type of stone.

clue.text: What opponents of ChatGPT etc may do in the sticks down under

definitions.text: What opponents of ChatGPT etc may do
definitions.meaning: first meaning: jeer at artificial intelligence, read as two words
second meaning: New Zealand slang for the remote back country

clue.text: Tailed Balkan resident, tailing group flying lower

parts.note: BA is British Airways
a Serb, docked of its last letter

explanation.definitionFit: Baser is the comparative of base, meaning lower in rank, worth or morality.

clue.text: Conservative in wing of building greeting emissary

indicators.note: in places the letter inside, here between two other pieces

parts.note: an el is a wing or extension of a building, a variant of ell

clue.text: Small parts of gold round outside of precise medical instrument

the letter O is round

clue.text: Old Nick is perhaps like a skeleton

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
to nick is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: The Devil, Old Nick, may be as thin as a skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Nick' reads as the Devil, but splits into O and Nick, British slang for to steal.

clue.text: Soldier astride horse from the East Indian region
